items.title: Long COVID burden in healthcare workers: a 12-month survey of 771 cases
items.abstract: Long COVID syndrome represents a significant public health concern, with healthcare workers constituting a population at particularly high risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection and subsequent persistent symptoms. To evaluate the prevalence of Long COVID syndrome in healthcare employees of IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo Foundation over a four-year time window from the pandemic onset. An anonymous survey was conducted among healthcare workers with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection since February 2020. Long COVID syndrome was defined as persistent symptoms lasting beyond 12 weeks from the acute infection, extending to 12 months or more. The Fisher exact test and the McNemar test were used to compare prevalences between groups and over time, respectively. Unsupervised learning techniques were used for identifying patient aggregation. Among 771 respondents (response rate 41.41% of employees with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection), the overall Long COVID syndrome cumulative prevalence (participants experiencing symptoms at any time point) was 27.9% (215/771; 95% CI: 24.7–31.2%), with point prevalence decreasing over time: 26.0% (95% CI 23.0–29.0%) at 3 months, 20.0% (95% CI 17.0–23.0%) at 6 months, and 16.0% (95% CI 14.0–19.0%) at 12 months post-infection. Significant associations were found with job position ( p = 0.004), with nurses showing the highest prevalence (35.0%). Fatigue, joint and muscle pain, concentration troubles, and memory difficulties emerged as the most persistent symptoms over time. Long COVID syndrome affects more than one-quarter of healthcare workers with previous SARS-CoV-2 infection, with symptom persistence demonstrating a gradual decline over time. These findings have important implications for occupational health management and workforce planning in healthcare settings.

items.title: Machine psychology for language models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

items.title: Magnitude of Primary Knee Osteoarthritis among the Healthcare Workers at BMU
items.abstract: Background: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a leading cause of disability among older adults and is increasingly recognized as a significant occupational health issue, especially among healthcare workers who are frequently exposed to repetitive knee strain. This study aims to identify the burden of primary knee osteoarthritis (KOA) among healthcare workers at a tertiary care institution in Bangladesh. Objective: The present study aimed to assess the magnitude and associated factors of primary knee osteoarthritis (KOA) among healthcare workers at BMU. Materials and Methods: This cross-sectional study included 185 healthcare workers selected by simple random sampling at BMU. Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) was diagnosed using the 2016 ACR clinical criteria. Data were collected using a modified and Bangla-adapted COPCORD questionnaire, including PHQ-9 and B-HAQ-DI tools. Anthropometric measurements were taken to calculate BMI. Data were analyzed using SPSS v23.0 with appropriate statistical tests; a p-value <0.05 was considered significant. Results: Among 185 healthcare workers, 42.2% were diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis (KOA), and 40% had a B-HAQ-DI score ≥0.8, indicating functional disability. Most KOA cases (57.7%) were female, and mild disability was the most common severity (28.9%). KOA prevalence was similar across physicians (40.5%), nurses (43.1%), and supporting staff (44%). Age was significantly associated with KOA (p = 0.034), with the highest prevalence in the 41–50 age group. Logistic regression identified increasing age (OR 1.064, p = 0.003) and female sex (OR 2.153, p = 0.020) as independent predictors. Conclusion: Knee osteoarthritis was prevalent among healthcare workers, with age and female sex as key predictors, highlighting the need for early intervention and preventive strategies in this population J Dhaka National Med. items.title: Making Feedback Quality Visible to Instructors: An AI-Supported Learning Analytics Dashboard Linking Peer Code Review to Pedagogical Action in Programming Education
items.abstract: Peer code review is widely used in programming and software engineering education, but its instructional value depends on the quality of student feedback rather than review completion alone. In large classes, instructors can readily monitor participation but lack scalable methods for assessing whether feedback is relevant, concrete, and constructive, limiting opportunities for timely instructional intervention. To address this gap, this study developed and evaluated the Review Engagement Graph (REG), an instructor focused learning analytics dashboard that integrates multilabel artificial intelligence classification of feedback quality with interactive network visualization. REG operationalizes feedback quality across three independent dimensions and translates five recurring visual patterns into corresponding pedagogical actions while preserving instructor judgment. The system was evaluated in two studies. Study 1 compared seven classification models spanning traditional machine learning, deep learning, fine-tuned transformers, and prompted large language models using 2,398 peer review comments independently annotated by two experts. Fine-tuned RoBERTa achieved the strongest overall performance, with a macro F1 score of 0.828. Study 2 evaluated REG with instructors and teaching assistants through scenario-based sessions. REG achieved a mean System Usability Scale score of 81.13, exceeding the benchmark of 68, and a mean perceived usefulness score of 4.31 out of 5. These findings demonstrate that AI classified feedback quality indicators can be transformed into actionable visual evidence through a pattern to action framework that supports timely and informed instructor decision making.

items.title: Measuring Interpersonal Differences Between Humans and HDTs Across Roles in Simulated Search and Rescue
items.abstract: Search and rescue is a team operation where uncertainty and hazards can fracture coordination and safety. Integrative stacks fusing information systems, UAVs, and robots can rebuild situational awareness and reduce exposure, but they are mostly passive. AI agents now show emergent goal pursuit through planning, self-correction, and replanning from noisy observations. It is unclear whether a human digital twin communicates interpersonally like a human under the same role-bounded information constraints. In this paper, we compare humans and HDTs in a role-conditioned, attribute-matched search and rescue simulation, quantifying nine-category responses for Engineer, Medic, and Transporter roles. We find distinct role-driven interaction signatures and a consistent human–HDT shift, with fewer questions and explicit agreements, offset by role-specific neutral stability and socioemotional support. The implication is that HDTs should better balance support with questioning and agreeing behaviors that humans rely on to confirm shared understanding and reach decisions in search and rescue.

items.abstract: Digital transformation in the world of education requires teachers to be able to adapt to technological developments while developing learning that is creative, innovative, and in accordance with the needs of students. This community service activity aims to improve teachers' competence in utilizing digital technology as a medium and learning resource and encourage the creation of more interactive and student-centered learning. Activities are carried out through socialization, training, direct practice, discussion, and mentoring. Activity materials include the use of digital platforms and applications for learning, the development of interactive learning media, the wise use of artificial intelligence (AI), and strategies for designing digital-based creative learning activities. The results of the activity show an increase in teachers' understanding and skills in selecting, using, and developing digital technology to support the learning process. Teachers are also able to produce more interesting, interactive, and contextual media designs and learning activities. This activity shows that digital transformation is not only related to mastery of technology, but also to teachers' ability to integrate technology, pedagogy, and creativity to create meaningful learning experiences. Thus, strengthening teachers' digital competencies needs to be carried out in a sustainable manner so that teachers are able to become creative, adaptive, and innovative educators in facing educational changes in the digital era.

items.title: Memory, Meaning and Consciousness
items.abstract: The human brain, and large language models, must retain, integrate and access huge quantities of information. The retained information depends upon the details of the encoding. The integration depends on elaborate connectivity. The access depends on a relationship to the entire database that includes the meanings and encoded information. The irreducible tension between the micro details of encoding information, and the total database perspective required for meaning, can be resolved only by an analytic tool, like the informational entropy of all or part of the data. Reified quantum mechanics, with a mechanism to resolve indeterminacy, can be viewed as a model of Panpsychism (Remler, 2026a) with the necessary analytic tools. This model provides a rational framework to understand evolution, with the rising centrality of negative entropy, and the massive encephalization manifest in human beings. The result is a scientifically based, conceptual model of the high-level human brain function including Consciousness and the range of Subjectivity.

items.title: Metacognitive disengagement and knowledge innovation quality in human–AI collaboration: the mediating role of cognitive offloading and the moderating roles of task complexity and AI literacy
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is fundamentally reshaping the cognitive conditions of knowledge innovation. While human–AI collaboration improves the efficiency of knowledge production, it may also induce creators to outsourcing cognitive work to AI systems. This study conceptualized this tendency as task-level metacognitive disengagement, defined as the immediate reduction of planning, monitoring, and reflection within a specific AI-assisted task, and, drawing on metacognition theory, cognitive offloading theory and self-regulated learning theory, examined its impact on knowledge innovation quality, its psychological mechanism, and boundary conditions through four complementary experiments. Experiment 1 showed that higher AI assistance significantly increased metacognitive disengagement. Experiment 2 revealed that cognitive offloading partially mediated the relationship between AI assistance and metacognitive disengagement. Experiment 3 confirmed the negative effect of cognitive offloading on knowledge innovation quality, specifically on novelty, usefulness, and developability, with metacognitive disengagement partially mediating this effect. Experiment 4 tested the proposed moderated mediation model and found that task complexity strengthened, whereas individual AI literacy weakened, the negative indirect effect of cognitive offloading on knowledge innovation quality through metacognitive disengagement. These findings reveal a hidden cognitive cost behind the efficiency gains of human–AI collaboration and provide empirical evidence and theoretical implications for cultivating innovative talent and designing human–AI collaborative mechanisms in the era of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Metadata Automation and Enrichment Using Machine Learning
items.abstract: This chapter examines how machine learning is transforming metadata automation and enrichment across research infrastructures, libraries, and data repositories. Synthesizing natural language processing, computer vision, large language models, and knowledge graph approaches, it analyzes how automated subject indexing, entity extraction, image captioning, author disambiguation, schema crosswalks, and ontology learning address persistent metadata quality deficits at scale. A machine learning enrichment pipeline model and a taxonomy of ML approaches are introduced, alongside a comparative modality table and performance bubble chart. The chapter critically examines FAIR data alignment, ethical governance, and implementation barriers.

items.title: Mobile-First & Responsive Cartographic De-sign in a Moment of Emergent Artificial Intelli-gence: Update on an ICA Research Agenda
items.abstract: Abstract. Here, we present and update a research agenda on mobile-first and responsive cartographic design published in the Journal of Location Based Services in 2024. We first introduce our collective process within the ICA (International Cartographic Association) to develop a set of three research agendas articles on mobile cartography that span user issues, technology issues, and design issues related to mobile maps and visualizations. We then describe a partial design space and 20 related research challenges from our assigned perspective of mobile map and visualization design. We then employ the 2024 research agenda as an analytical framework to review recent literature and reflect on emerging challenges and opportunities for research and development on mobile cartography given the fast-paced innovations in GeoAI (Geospatial Artificial Intelligence) since 2024. We conclude with priority considerations for integrating mobile cartography and GeoAI.

items.title: Modeling ESG Performance Drivers in the Shipping Industry: An LLM‐Assisted q‐ ROFRS‐Delphi‐WINGS‐FCM Framework for Causal Analysis and Simulation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The shipping industry plays a vital role in global trade and also exerts significant environmental and social pressures due to high fuel consumption, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and intensive port activities. Implementing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices offers a strategic pathway to enhance sustainability performance in this sector; however, it remains difficult to determine which managerial and operational actions can most effectively drive improvements in ESG performance. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel framework that integrates a large language model (LLM), an extended q‐ rung orthopair fuzzy rough set ( q‐ ROFRS)‐based Delphi‐weighted influence nonlinear gauge system (WINGS) model, and a fuzzy cognitive mapping (FCM) simulation. This approach systematically identifies critical success factors (CSFs), analyzes their cause–effect relationships, and simulates their dynamic influence on ESG performance in the shipping industry. The findings reveal that six CSFs, including structured board oversight, global policy engagement, comprehensive legal compliance framework, employee‐centric culture, effective communication strategy, and integrated water resource management, serve as key causal drivers within the ESG system. FCM‐based scenario simulations suggest that full activation of these modeled drivers could substantially improve projected ESG performance under the assumed scenario conditions. This research offers a dual contribution: Theoretically, it extends fuzzy decision‐making and AI‐driven causal modeling to complex sustainability systems; practically, it provides actionable guidance for shipping companies and policymakers to strengthen ESG integration, meet the International Maritime Organization's net‐zero targets, and advance the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

items.title: Multi-Agent Task Automation System
items.abstract: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) offer an effective approach for solving complex and large-scale problems in distributed artificial intelligence by dividing them into smaller subtasks handled by multiple autonomous agents. Each agent can perceive its environment, process information, make decisions, and perform actions according to its assigned objectives. Agents communicate, collaborate, and coordinate to achieve individual and collective goals, providing advantages such as scalability, adaptability, flexibility, robustness, and fault tolerance. The proposed Multi-Agent Task Automation System uses heterogeneous agents dynamically assigned tasks according to their capabilities, resource availability, current workload, task priority, execution cost, and contextual relevance. A mediator-based coordination mechanism supports agent discovery and task routing while allowing direct peer-to-peer communication when necessary. Dynamic task allocation and load balancing help distribute work efficiently. Reinforcement learning can enhance agent decision-making by allowing agents to learn from feedback and improve their strategies over time. The system also incorporates fault detection, recovery, authentication, secure communication, and trust evaluation to improve reliability and security. The implementation uses Python, AutoGen, large language models, APIs, and external tools, with structured message passing enabling agents to interact and execute tasks collaboratively. Tasks are initiated through user input and processed using iterative communication, reasoning, and tool execution. The proposed approach demonstrates the potential of MAS to improve task execution efficiency, response time, resource utilization, adaptability, scalability, and fault tolerance compared with traditional centralized approaches. However, communication overhead, coordination complexity, security risks, synchronization, and efficient task allocation remain important challenges.

items.title: Multi-Aspect Digital Twin for Critical Infrastructures
items.abstract: This chapter highlights the evolution of digital twins from passive data repositories to intelligent systems capable of contextual reasoning, supporting informed decision-making. We introduce the multi-aspect digital twin named MADT4BC, a core DYNABIC component designed to address the observability challenge and increase situational awareness in multi-scale critical infrastructures through AI-based assisting technology. MADT4BC reads and stores heterogeneous data streams from the physical infrastructure, connecting these to a semantically rich digital representation of real infrastructure using knowledge graphs. In response to user requests, AI agents are deployed to operate on top of the knowledge graph: creating, extracting, contextualizing, and reasoning over the collected operational data and the asset information to provide timely responses. We validate MADT4BC through one real-world use case, showcasing both knowledge creation and extraction abilities.

items.abstract: "Munzur University’s Rare Earth Elements (REE) Operational Program addresses Türkiye’s R&D, product development, education, capacity-building, and regional development objectives in the fields of strategic raw materials and advanced technology applications through a holistic approach. Within the scope of Munzur University’s regional development-oriented mission differentiation, its area of specialization has been defined as “Strategic Raw Materials and Advanced Technology Applications.” Accordingly, rare earth elements, critical minerals, advanced materials, recycling, chemical purification, environmentally friendly production, and the development of high valueadded technological products have become priority areas of work. The project titled “Enhancing the Research and Innovation Capacity of Türkiye in Rare Earth Elements,” co-financed by the European Union and the Republic of Türkiye, aims to contribute to the establishment of a sustainable REE supply chain in Türkiye. The final beneficiary of the project is the General Directorate of Industry (SGM), while its partners are Munzur University Rare Earth Elements Application and Research Center (MUNTEAM) and the General Directorate of Mineral Research and Exploration (MTA). Within the scope of the project, the MUNTEAM building was allocated, laboratory infrastructure was established, research partnerships were developed, and the center began carrying out activities in analysis, accreditation, education, R&D, product development, and business development. The current status of the program is not limited solely to the establishment of laboratory infrastructure. Projects supported by The Scientific and Technological Research Council of Türkiye (TUBITAK), the Presidency of Strategy and Budget, and collaborations with various universities cover a wide range of fields, including ore enrichment, chemical purification, solvent extraction, bioleaching, recycling, advanced alloys, optoelectronic materials, catalysts, biomedical applications, and data analytics. In addition, training programs for R&D professionals, the critical minerals optimization team, and data science and artificial intelligence-based analytical approaches strengthen the program’s human resource capacity and methodological competence. As a result, Munzur University’s REE Operational Program holds a strategic position in terms of Türkiye’s critical mineral independence, green transition, defense industry, e-mobility, digital technologies, and circular economy objectives. Internationalization, accreditation, open innovation, industrial integration, and the establishment of new graduate programs and institutes are of critical importance for the sustainability of the program."

items.title: Mutual Information Analysis of Employment-Course Score Relationships for Curriculum Optimization in Higher Vocational Traditional Chinese Pharmacy
items.abstract: Against rising graduate employment pressure and the widespread application of digital technology across industries, the curriculum of higher vocational Traditional Chinese Pharmacy (TCP) fails to fully match the competency requirements of actual jobs. This research intends to quantitatively analyze the correlation between students’ course scores and employment performance, offering data support for curriculum revision and optimization in vocational colleges. Using data from 236 TCP graduates, the study classified employment destinations into six types and converted them into binary employment variables. Mutual Information (MI) was employed to quantify the nonlinear correlation between 49 course scores and employment results. Combined with a Monte Carlo-assisted elimination algorithm, the research filtered out courses with no statistical connection to employment. Repeated random sampling ensured stable numerical results and course rankings. The findings show that core TCP professional courses do not occupy leading positions in the MI ranking. Sensitivity tests by removing average grades further verified the reliability of the conclusions. This study proves MI is a valid tool for exploring links between courses and employment, while pointing out its limitation: MI only reflects correlation instead of causality. It is recommended that curriculum teams refer to MI rankings, align course design with talent training goals and industry needs, and add digital competency courses including artificial intelligence and big data analysis to adapt to industrial upgrading.

items.title: My daughter knows over 21 people that have died from drug overdose or suicide: cross-sector rural provider perspectives on adverse childhood experiences
items.abstract: Background Cumulative exposure to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) is associated with an increased risk of substance use, overdose, and suicide. Rural children are more likely to experience most ACEs. There is limited literature contextualizing rural individuals’ experiences with ACEs. Public Health 3.0 calls for multisector partner engagement to generate collective impact. The purpose of this study was to evaluate rural providers’ perspectives on challenges and recommendations for ACEs mitigation in their community from a cross-sector context. Participants and setting Participants were 74 providers enrolled in an online ACEs training. Participants lived and/or worked in five rural Missouri counties with high drug overdose death rates. Methods This was a conventional content analysis of written responses to structured discussion prompts from three training modules. Analysis included familiarization, inductive identification of major codes, and refinement of codes, followed by independent coding by two authors until consensus, and reporting major patterns. Artificial intelligence supported preliminary code development. An adapted Sequential Intercept Model (SIM) framework organized challenges and recommendations by setting. Results Results included personal stories about how ACEs impacted their communities through overdose, suicide, homelessness, unemployment, and adverse health effects. Settings included schools, government, healthcare, daycares, criminal justice, Extension, fire departments, libraries, and nonprofits. Participants recommended expanding the ACEs definition to include satanic abuse, bullying, incest, war, genocide, military family stressors, and death of a loved one. Intervention recommendations included whole-family interventions, community-wide training, trauma-informed training, expanded access to treatment, classes in prison/jails, and fostering positive childhood experiences. Conclusion Community voice is necessary to contextualize setting-specific insights that inform development of upstream interventions appropriate for and tailored to the community. Participants identified both strategies that could be incorporated into everyday practice—including empathy, listening, providing judgment-free and safe spaces, providing food for children experiencing hunger, encouraging positive childhood experiences, mentoring, and connecting individuals with resources for food, shelter, clothing, and mental health—and broader structural changes that may require policy-level action. The adapted SIM organizes these concepts.

items.title: Navigating the Crosscurrent of Educational Influencers
items.abstract: While federal reform movements have shaped modern public education through legislation, education has also been subject to dramatic social, political, and technological pressures. In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic forced schools to adapt to distance learning within days to weeks. Virtual schooling came with benefits as well as challenges. When in-person instruction resumed, many classrooms were far more reliant on technology than they had been prior to the pandemic. Similarly, the widespread adoption of generative AI technology, beginning in 2022, has had both positive and negative consequences for education. Throughout these massive social and technological shifts, new political debates in education have become prominent. Schools are facing political pressure at the local and state levels, financial pressure from the popularization of vouchers, and social pressure from backlash against Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion measures. This chapter describes the current social, technological, and political environments which future-thinking leaders must respond.

items.title: Often Correct, Not Reliably Correct: A Blinded Audit of GPT-5.2 as Guideline-Decision Support for a Rare Cancer (Penile Squamous Cell Carcinoma)
items.abstract: Objective: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as guideline-decision support in oncology, but most validation has occurred in common cancers, where clinicians can usually recognize errors. The safety-critical setting is the opposite — rare cancers, where local expertise is limited, and errors may go unrecognized. Whether common-cancer concordance reflects the reliability needed there is unclear. Methods: We benchmarked GPT-5.2 against the EAU-ASCO 2025 Penile Cancer Guidelines using 100 guideline-derived questions across five domains and three zero-shot prompting strategies, yielding 300 responses. Two experienced urologists, blinded to prompt identity, scored concordance on a 3-point scale and classified errors as hallucination, omission, temporal, or reasoning. The primary analysis was a mixed-effects ordinal logistic regression with question as a random intercept; a cluster-robust logistic regression served as sensitivity. Reporting followed TRIPOD-LLM. Results: GPT-5.2 was fully concordant in 236 of 300 responses (78.7%; 95% confidence interval, 73.7–82.9; weighted κ=0.914). Prompt strategy did not improve performance (role-play +3 percentage points; 95% credible interval, −2 to +9). The domain effect was not robust once between-question clustering was modeled. Among 64 non-concordant responses, omission predominated (47.7%) and reasoning errors followed (37.5%); in treatment, omission accounted for 68.0% of errors, including loss of guideline-specified detail. Four questions were uniformly discordant across all three prompts. Conclusion: Headline concordance overstated clinical reliability. The clinically informative finding was not the overall accuracy but the structure of failure — omission of decision-critical treatment detail and stable errors. Prompt engineering did not rescue performance. Current LLM output may assist orientation in rare-cancer decision pathways but is not ready as stand-alone guideline-decision support.

items.title: One Photograph, Several Readings: Checking an AI Prediction of Cancer Patient Survival Time from a Face Photograph Against the Camera and Software's Own Settings
items.abstract: A foundation model trained on over 40 million face photographs can now estimate biological age and predict the survival of cancer patients from a single photograph. Today the photograph is taken once and the model gives one survival score, with no sign of how firm that score is. This concept note describes a simple check that can sit on top of such a model. From the photograph that is already stored, the computer makes two to four versions by changing only the photograph's own processing settings, within the range the camera, the capture software and the clinic permit. The same model reads every version, unchanged. If the survival scores stay together, the prediction is firm. If they spread out, it depends on a setting. One number, the spread value, shows which case it is. A computer-decided shunting action then moves the case that needs care to the front of the clinician's list while all other cases carry on. The check adds no device, no visit and no change to the model, and the decision stays with the clinician. The note explains the method in plain steps, shows how it speaks to the lighting and image-quality limitation named by the authors of the published model, and compares it with earlier work and patents. Keywords: survival prediction, face photograph, biological age, AI, uncertainty, robustness, early warning, shunting action, foundation model

items.abstract: In higher education, students’ needs are becoming increasingly diverse, making it insufficient to support them solely through general recommendations and traditional monitoring methods. An important task of tutoring is to recognise these differences, maintain regular communication with students, and help them manage their own learning pathways consciously.

items.title: Opt-IncpResN-V2: A Hyper-Optimized Framework for Image Quality Enhancement and Feature-Rich Content-Based Image Retrieval
items.abstract: Content-Based Image Retrieval (CBIR) has been rapidly developed and implemented in different sectors connected to computer vision and artificial intelligence due to the growth of the Internet and the prevalence of digital devices. An input picture can efficiently and effectively retrieve related images from a large-scale database. Over the last ten years, much work has been done to develop new CBIR theories and models, and numerous efficient CBIR algorithms have been developed. Finding identical pictures in an extensive collection that match the query picture is made more accessible through content-based image retrieval. Ranking the pictures for retrieval usually involves considering the representative feature similarities between the dataset and query pictures. This study introduces Deep Learning (DL)-based Opt-IncpResN-V2, a hyper-optimized framework designed to enhance image quality and enable feature-rich CBIR. With the proliferation of digital images and the expansion of image databases, efficient image retrieval methods are essential. Unlike traditional text-based image retrieval (TBIR), which relies on manual keyword annotation, CBIR retrieves images based on visual features such as colour, texture, and shape. Our framework incorporates an image quality improvement process during preprocessing, including noise reduction, edge detection, normalisation, and contrast enhancement. Features are extracted using the Inception-ResNet-V2 technique, and classification accuracy is improved using the Artificial Flora Optimisation Algorithm (AFOA). Images are then classified using DenseNet-264, and hyperparameters are optimised using the Improved Hippopotamus Optimisation Algorithm (IHOA). The proposed approach is evaluated on four benchmark datasets: Kvasir, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Corel-1k. Experimental results demonstrate superior performance compared to state-of-the-art techniques, achieving accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-scores exceeding 99% across all datasets.

items.title: Optimization of MSME Digital Promotion Through Artificial Intelligence Training and Mentoring in Mendalo Laut Village
items.abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Mendalo Laut Village still face limitations in utilizing digital technology to support business identity development and promotion. This community service activity aimed to improve MSME actors’ understanding and provide practical experience in utilizing Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly ChatGPT, as a tool for developing ideas and creating digital promotional materials. The activity was conducted on July 15, 2026, at the Mendalo Laut Village Office Hall and involved 16 MSME actors engaged in food and service businesses. The methods included material presentation, discussion, hands-on practice, and mentoring. Participants were introduced to the use of ChatGPT for developing prompts and creating concepts for business logos, posters, banners, and product flyers. The results showed that participants were enthusiastic about the training and gained initial experience in utilizing ChatGPT to support digital promotion. Some participants were able to follow the practical activities with guidance, while others required more intensive assistance due to differences in digital skills. This activity served as an initial step in encouraging the use of AI to support more independent and sustainable digital promotion among MSMEs.

items.title: Oversight asymmetry in AI-assisted clinical documentation: a comparative-abductive study using neonatal discharge as a test context
items.abstract: Background Human oversight is widely treated as a safeguard for clinical artificial intelligence (AI), yet a reviewer may remain formally responsible without having the knowledge, time, or authority required to verify generated documentation. We develop “oversight asymmetry” as a prospective governance diagnosis and use neonatal discharge as a theoretical test context for responsible digital paediatrics, not as an observed setting of AI use. Methods We conducted a comparative-abductive, netnographically informed qualitative study of 64 public Reddit threads posted between 2021 and April 2026, with comment trees retrieved under pre-specified extraction parameters. The threads contained 2,848 comments and replies from 1,723 pseudonymised accounts in nursing, neonatal, paediatric, medicine, and health informatics communities, and 49 threads contributed to the final themes. A discharge and transition-home stream, drawn mainly from general nursing communities, and a smaller AI documentation and communication stream were analysed separately using reflexive thematic analysis before abductive comparison. Professional role was attributed only where contributors explicitly self-positioned. Results Discharge readiness was described as depending on knowledge distributed across records, professionals, bedside observation, and families, while responsibility for release could become concentrated. Frontline responsibility was separable from institutional authority, although several accounts described distributed oversight that worked because escalation was available. In four anchor threads from two communities, AI documentation discussions described faster drafting alongside residual source checking and correction, and a narrower set of accounts described reconstruction of missing clinical rationale. Workload accounts, together with AI-linked predictions in two threads, suggest that anticipated efficiency may be converted into higher workload before residual verification work is removed. We propose that oversight becomes vulnerable when verification responsibility and demand exceed epistemic access, protected time or consequential authority. Conclusion Oversight asymmetry identifies a prospective mechanism through which nominal human review may fail to constitute meaningful oversight. Responsible paediatric artificial intelligence governance should measure residual verification work, preserve provenance and access to family and bedside context, protect review time, and provide effective output-level and system-level escalation authority before automation is treated as additional capacity. The study generates propositions for prospective evaluation and does not claim that artificial intelligence-assisted neonatal discharge was directly observed.

items.title: Owning what one did not make: psychological ownership, agency, and the authorship legitimation deficit in human–AI co-creation
items.abstract: Authorship can align three relations to a work: experiencing it as one’s own, feeling like the agent behind it, and standing answerable for it. Effortful engagement can support this alignment, an arrangement this article calls the labor nexus of authorship, but direction, selection, editing, and authority over release also matter. Generative artificial intelligence can separate initial-production effort from the resulting product without uniformly weakening ownership, agency, or responsibility. This conceptual analysis specifies an authorship legitimation deficit as a mismatch between a particular authorship designation and the experiential or contribution-based grounds expected to support it under prior domain criteria. Separate ownership, agency, and community-warrant profiles distinguish an unsupported sole-creator claim from a supported editorial role, even when the person’s contribution and experience are unchanged. Historical precedents locate the problem within delegated and distributed making. The main contribution is a role-relative conceptual classification. Conditional relational hypotheses concern refusal or qualification of authorship (P4) and later recognition of alternative contributions (P6); agency and observer credit-blame hypotheses (P5a/P5b) concern constituent concepts rather than effects of the deficit. Market dependence suppresses observable disavowal when qualification threatens income; perceived system agency conditions felt answerability while assigned release duties remain fixed. Contribution records may assist later recognition but do not guarantee it. The framework identifies when a role exceeds its grounds while preserving supported AI-assisted authorship and accountability for release.

items.title: Parental Emotion Regulation and Children’s Mental Health Across Cultural Contexts: A Study of Immigrant and Non-Immigrant Families in the United States
items.abstract: Parental emotion regulation plays a critical role in shaping children's psychological adjustment, emotional resilience, and mental health outcomes. However, variations in cultural orientation, immigration experiences, family stress, and parenting practices complicate the identification of these relationships across immigrant and non-immigrant populations in the United States. This study proposes a novel Culturally Adaptive Parental Emotion Regulation and Mental Health Prediction Algorithm (CAPER-MH) to investigate the relationships between parental emotion regulation, cultural adaptation, family socioeconomic characteristics, and children's mental health. The proposed framework integrates multilevel statistical modelling, machine learning, and explainable artificial intelligence to estimate psychological risk while accounting for cultural heterogeneity and family-level dependencies. The study is designed to analyse parental emotion regulation difficulties, cognitive reappraisal, expressive suppression, acculturative stress, parent-child relationships, and children's internalizing and externalizing symptoms using validated psychometric instruments.

items.title: Partnership Strategies for Transforming Travel Experiences With Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the travel industry has fundamentally redefined how organizations collaborate, compete, and deliver value. This chapter examines the various types of strategic alliances and partnerships that relate to AI-driven travel solutions, including the juristic relationships created when airlines and hotel chains, online travel agencies (OTAs), software providers, and startup companies, develop AI ecosystems together. Drawing on partnership theory, resource-based views, and platform economics, the research will explore how the motivations, structures, and governance models of these alliances. The research analyses the role of data sharing agreements, including partnership agreements, co-innovation labs, and intermediate integration of Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) as means of accelerating AI adoption and creating digital transformation. Last, the chapter will discuss such challenges as data privacy, competitive cannibalism, and trust asymmetries between competing legacy firms and technology operators.

items.title: Patient trust in health education attributed to generative artificial intelligence versus a physician: a randomized survey study of pregnant and postpartum women
items.abstract: Abstract Objective To compare patient trust in educational health contentand the physician providing it, when authorship is attributed to a physician or generative artificial intelligence (AI). Materials and Methods In a preregistered randomized, parallel survey study, participants read a health education article. Individuals were randomized to 1 of 4 conditions, attributing authorship of an identical article to (1) a physician author, (2) generative AI, (3) a physician assisted by AI (hybrid authorship), or (4) no author. Pregnant or postpartum English-speaking US adults (n = 400) were recruited in August-October 2025 via an online survey panel. Eighty percent passed timing and attention checks. Participants rated article engagement, content trust, and trust in the (hypothetical) recommending physician with Likert-scales. Bonferroni corrections were applied to post hoc pairwise comparisons (α = 0.05). Results Among participants who correctly recalled authorship (n = 195), AI-only authorship was associated with lower trust in content (mean, 9.43 vs 11.11; P = .001) and the recommending physician (mean, 8.93 vs 10.84; P = .03) compared with physician-only authorship, while hybrid authorship did not differ significantly from physician-only authorship for either outcome (content: P = .08; physician: P > .99). Sensitivity analyses including all participants (n = 321) were generally consistent with the primary findings. Engagement did not differ significantly across conditions in the primary analytic sample. Discussion As generative AI becomes increasingly integrated into clinical care, how AI involvement and physician oversight are communicated to patients could have important implications for patient trust. Conclusion AI authorship was associated with reduced trust in patient-facing education despite identical, clinician-written content.

items.abstract: Akselerasi perkembangan teknologi Artificial Intelligence (AI) yang masif menuntut peningkatan kapasitas digital siswa kejuruan agar adaptif. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan untuk meningkatkan literasi digital dan keterampilan praktis siswa SMK Semen Gresik dalam mengembangkan website menggunakan AI serta mengevaluasi luaran kodenya secara kritis. Metode pelaksanaan diorganisasikan melalui transfer pengetahuan dan demonstrasi perumusan instruksi (prompt engineering) berbasis kerangka CRAFT (Context, Role, Action, Format, Tone). Program ini diselenggarakan pada 24 April 2026 dengan melibatkan siswa konsentrasi keahlian Rekayasa Perangkat Lunak (RPL). Hasil kegiatan mengindikasikan bahwa pemanfaatan AI mampu mengakselerasi alur perancangan antarmuka dan arsitektur halaman web secara signifikan. Siswa terbukti mampu mentransformasikan kebutuhan spesifikasi pengguna menjadi prompt terstruktur serta melakukan refinasi dan modifikasi mandiri terhadap basis kode yang dihasilkan. Integrasi AI ini terbukti memperkokoh pemahaman logika automasi proses digital tanpa mengeliminasi kendali kognitif dan daya kritis siswa (human-in-the-loop) dalam siklus pengembangan perangkat lunak.

items.title: Pengaruh Penerapan Model Blended Learning Berbantuan MagicSchool AI terhadap Hasil Belajar Siswa Kelas VII pada Mata Pelajaran TIK SMPI Al Ishlah Bukittinggi
items.abstract: Blended learning supported by artificial intelligence offers an alternative approach to improving students’ learning outcomes in Information and Communication Technology (ICT). However, the combined use of blended learning and MagicSchool AI for digital literacy instruction at the junior high school level requires further empirical investigation. This study aimed to analyze the effect of a blended learning model supported by MagicSchool AI on seventh-grade students’ ICT learning outcomes at SMPI Al Ishlah Bukittinggi. The study employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest control group design. The participants comprised 56 students divided into experimental and control groups, with 28 students in each group. Data were collected through achievement tests administered before and after the intervention and analyzed using an independent-samples t test. The results showed that the experimental group’s mean score increased from 51.07 on the pretest to 81.96 on the posttest, while the control group’s mean score increased from 53.39 to 67.50. Hypothesis testing revealed a significant difference in learning outcomes between the two groups (p < .001). These findings provide empirical support for the potential of blended learning supported by MagicSchool AI to improve students’ learning outcomes in digital literacy. In practical terms, the findings may inform teachers’ design of ICT instruction that integrates face-to-face activities and the use of artificial intelligence. Future research should involve more schools and compare the contributions of individual instructional components to clarify their roles in students’ attainment of learning outcomes.

items.title: Perceived algorithmic control and courier safety risk in last-mile delivery: a transparency paradox
items.abstract: Purpose Drawing on job demands–resources theory, this study examines how perceived algorithmic operations control (PAC) relates to couriers' safety-compliance risk. PAC denotes algorithmic oversight: feeling monitored, directed and constrained by platform algorithms. The risk is physical: unsafe riding that can cause crashes. Two mechanisms are tested: system-triggered interruptions that fragment attention (a job demand) and reduced autonomy to adapt safely (a lost resource). Boundary conditions are dependence on platform income and visibility-based transparency, a widely advocated remedy. Design/methodology/approach In an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, interviews and field observations informed the measures. A cross-sectional questionnaire survey of 344 food-delivery couriers in China was analysed using regression-based moderated-mediation tests. Riders' forum posts, produced independently of the survey, served to triangulate (cross-check) the survey constructs. Findings Stronger PAC is associated with more self-reported risky riding (incidents were not measured), partly through more interruptions and lower autonomy. Economic dependence weakens the interruption pathway but strengthens autonomy loss. Transparency strengthens both pathways, linking PAC to more interruptions and greater autonomy loss. This is the transparency paradox: a presumed remedy unintentionally amplifies risk. Originality/value Algorithmic management operates through adjustable system parameters: how often platform data interrupt couriers and how much discretion they retain. To cut risk without losing efficiency, platforms can pace notifications, freeze mid-route reassignments, restore discretion through exception handling and pair transparency with actionable options. For regulators, disclosure mandates alone may not make delivery safer.

items.title: Perceived Craftsmanship Spirit and AI Technology Adoption Behavior Among University Faculty Members: A Moderated Mediation Model
items.abstract: University faculty members’ adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies is important to the digital transformation of higher education, yet the motivational mechanisms associated with such behavior remain insufficiently understood. Drawing on self-determination theory (SDT), and the job demands–resources (JD–R) model, this study used a sample of 374 university faculty members to examine, through a moderated mediation model, the mechanism underlying the relationship between perceived craftsmanship spirit and AI technology adoption behavior. The results showed that perceived craftsmanship spirit significantly and positively predicted AI technology adoption behavior and that work engagement mediated this relationship. Challenge stressors negatively moderated the relationship between perceived craftsmanship spirit and work engagement and weakened the mediating effect of work engagement. These findings reveal the underlying pathway through which perceived craftsmanship spirit promotes AI technology adoption behavior and provide theoretical and practical implications for advancing the digital development and transformation of higher education.

items.title: Perceived Ratings of AI-Generated and Expert-Reviewed vs Clinician-Developed Virtual Cardiology Patient Scenarios Among Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Study
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Virtual patients (VPs) are widely used in medical education, but creating high-quality cases requires clinical expertise, iterative revision, and alignment with educational objectives. Generative AI may support VP authoring, but direct comparisons between AI-generated and clinician-developed cases delivered within the same educational setting remain limited. OBJECTIVE This study aimed to compare medical students’ learner-perceived ratings of 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed virtual cardiology patient scenario with those of 1 clinician-developed virtual cardiology patient scenario delivered through the same mobile platform. METHODS A randomized, participant-blinded 2-arm controlled study was conducted in October 2025 during scheduled fifth-year emergency medicine course sessions. Eligible participants were fifth-year medical students who had completed the cardiology course. Students were assigned 1:1 to complete either a clinician-developed VP (CD-VP; n=64) or a ChatGPT-generated VP (GPT-VP; n=67). Both scenarios followed a shared acute coronary syndrome blueprint and were delivered through the same mobile-optimized app (mobile VPs app [MobiViP]) with identical interface structure and branching logic. The GPT-VP was generated using GPT-5 and refined through iterative follow-up prompting under expert review; direct manual rewriting was prohibited. After completion, students completed a mandatory 19-item questionnaire covering realism and validity, cognitive load, self-reported learning and reflection, and engagement and satisfaction. Analyses included reliability testing, 1-sample tests against a neutral midpoint, Mann-Whitney U tests, and Spearman correlations. Full scenario content and development details are provided as multimedia appendices. RESULTS A total of 131 complete questionnaires were analyzed, with no item-level missing data. Mean subscale scores in the CD-VP group were 3.81 (SD 0.64) for realism and validity, 3.67 (SD 0.74) for cognitive load, 3.64 (SD 0.73) for self-reported learning and reflection, and 4.16 (SD 0.64) for engagement and satisfaction; corresponding GPT-VP scores were 4.11 (SD 0.56), 3.03 (SD 0.76), 3.86 (SD 0.77), and 4.28 (SD 0.58), respectively. Compared with the CD-VP, the GPT-VP received higher ratings for realism and validity (Mann-Whitney U=1503.0; P=.003) and lower cognitive load ratings, indicating a lower perceived burden (Mann-Whitney U=1070.5; P<.001). Self-reported learning and reflection showed a marginal difference between groups, with a higher rating for the GPT-VP (Mann-Whitney U=1719.0; P=.05), whereas engagement and satisfaction did not differ significantly (Mann-Whitney U=1922.5; P=.31). Internal consistency was acceptable to good for most subscales, although internal consistency for the realism and validity subscale in the GPT-VP group was moderate (Cronbach α=0.67). CONCLUSIONS In this single-center randomized study, 1 AI-generated, expert-reviewed cardiology VP scenario was rated similarly to or more favorably than 1 clinician-developed scenario in selected learner-perceived domains. Future research should expand to objective learning, retention, development workload, and scalability outcomes.

items.title: Performance Management and Workforce Analytics in Tourism
items.abstract: The fast adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in tourism management has fundamentally changed the way organizations handle human resources, performance, and utilize workforce data. This chapter explains how AI-based performance management systems and workforce analytics can be used in a versatile way in the tourism and hospitality industries. It relies on current empirical data and theoretical ideas to explore how machine learning algorithms, predictive analytics, and real-time data platforms are changing talent acquisition, employee performance appraisal, demand-based scheduling, and strategic workforce planning. The chapter also discusses the ethical issues of algorithmic bias, privacy, and employee autonomy, and the need to adopt hybrid human-AI governance frameworks. The practical implementation results are reflected in the case studies of large global tourism enterprises. The chapter ends with a discussion of future research directions and policy implications of sustainable, technology-enhanced people management in tourism.

items.title: Perspective Chapter: Digital versus Traditional Autopsy in Forensic Practice – Techniques, Applications and Future Directions
items.abstract: Autopsy, as a cornerstone of post-mortem investigation, has undergone significant evolution over the years. Traditional autopsy, characterised by manual examination and tissue sampling, has long been the gold standard for determining the cause of death and uncovering underlying pathologies. However, the emergence of digital autopsy, leveraging advanced imaging techniques and computational analysis, presents a promising alternative. This chapter provides a comprehensive comparison between traditional and digital autopsy, encompassing their methodologies, diagnostic accuracy, practicality, limitations, and ethical considerations. It focuses on how digital tools such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and digital imaging and communications in medicine (DICOM)-based visualisation reconstruct the human body’s structure into detailed, colour-coded three-dimensional models of the internal organs. The chapter further examines the impact of technological advancement on forensic pathology and explores the integration of digitalisation, artificial intelligence, and minimally invasive techniques into routine post-mortem practice. Its novelty lies in bringing conventional dissection-based autopsy and digital/virtual autopsy together within a single comparative framework, and in extending that framework to artificial intelligence and minimally invasive sampling. By elucidating the strengths and limitations of both approaches, it aims to guide forensic practitioners, pathologists, radiologists, policymakers, and researchers in making informed decisions regarding post-mortem examination methodologies. The chapter moves from foundational definitions through a technique-by-technique comparison to ethical and future considerations, and is intended primarily for forensic medicine trainees, pathologists, and medico-legal professionals.

items.title: PGNexus-AI: An Intelligent and Secure Natural-Language PostgreSQL Administration Framework
items.abstract: Modern teams depend on PostgreSQL for mission-critical workloads, yet administration is still done by hand-writing SQL in disconnected tools such as psql, pgAdmin and DBeaver, while AI assistants such as GitHub Copilot have no live connection to the database and cannot read its schema, execution plans or error output. LLM-generated SQL also introduces new injection-style security risks. This paper presents PGNexus-AI, a PostgreSQL-only desktop IDE that combines Google Gemini, Gemma 4 and GitHub Copilot behind a schema-grounded orchestration layer. It provides natural-language-to-SQL generation, execution-plan-driven query optimization, automatic error diagnosis and correction, and AI-generated schema documentation with column-relationship mapping. A defense-in-depth safety layer (parameterization, query preview and confirmation, read-only and sandbox execution, role-based scoping and injection screening) protects production databases, and GitHub integration version-controls SQL and migrations. We describe the architecture, methodology and an evaluation plan covering efficiency, reliability, optimization and security.

items.title: Pharmaceutical Quality Assurance: Principles, Regulatory Framework, Current Practices and Emerging Trends – A Review
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical quality assurance (QA) is a comprehensive and systematic approach designed to ensure that medicinal products consistently meet predetermined standards of quality, safety, identity, strength, purity and efficacy throughout their intended lifecycle. The contemporary pharmaceutical industry has moved beyond a predominantly end-product testing model toward integrated, science-based and risk-based quality management. Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), Pharmaceutical Quality Systems (PQS), Quality Risk Management (QRM), Quality by Design (QbD), validation, qualification, change control, deviation management, corrective and preventive action (CAPA), supplier qualification, documentation and data integrity constitute major components of modern pharmaceutical QA. International regulatory frameworks developed by the World Health Organization (WHO), International Council for Harmonisation (ICH), United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other regulatory bodies increasingly emphasize lifecycle management, continual improvement and reliable data. The 2024 tenth edition of the WHO pharmaceutical quality assurance compendium provides an updated global framework extending from pharmaceutical development and manufacturing to quality control and post-marketing surveillance. Recent advances in digitalization, artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), Process Analytical Technology (PAT), continuous manufacturing and advanced data analytics are further transforming pharmaceutical quality management. However, these technologies also introduce challenges related to validation, data integrity, cyber security, model governance and regulatory acceptance. This review discusses the fundamental concepts, major components, regulatory framework, implementation strategies, current challenges and emerging trends in pharmaceutical quality assurance. An integrated lifecycle-based QA system supported by scientific understanding, risk management, robust documentation, quality culture and appropriate technology is essential for ensuring consistent product quality and protecting patient safety.

items.title: Pharmacogenomics and Personalized Medicine: Translating Genetic Variation into Precision Therapeutics
items.abstract: Interindividual variability in drug response represents a persistent challenge in clinical pharmacology, contributing to therapeutic failure and adverse drug reactions (ADRs) in a substantial proportion of patients. Pharmacogenomics, the study of how genomic variation influences drug disposition and effects, has emerged as a transformative discipline bridging pharmacology and genomics.This review synthesizes contemporary evidence regarding the principles, clinical applications, technologies, and implementation frameworks of pharmacogenomics within the broader context of personalized medicine. Genetic polymorphisms affecting pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic pathways—particularly within cytochrome P450 enzymes, thiopurine methyltransferase, dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase, and human leukocyte antigen loci—demonstrate robust associations with drug efficacy and toxicity. Regulatory agencies including the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) have incorporated pharmacogenomic biomarkers into drug labeling, while the Clinical Pharmacogenetics Implementation Consortium (CPIC) and the Dutch Pharmacogenetics Working Group (DPWG) have issued actionable dosing guidelines for numerous gene-drug pairs. Despite compelling evidence, the transition from research to routine clinical practice remains heterogeneous globally, impeded by economic barriers, educational gaps, and ethical complexities surrounding genetic data.The integration of artificial intelligence, multi-omics platforms, and digital health infrastructure promises to accelerate pharmacogenomic adoption, yet successful implementation requires harmonized regulatory standards, equitable access across diverse populations, and systematic healthcare professional education. Pharmacogenomics stands poised to fundamentally redefine therapeutic paradigms, shifting from empirical prescribing to genotype-directed precision medicine.

items.title: Postural ergonomic risks during clinical dental training: A five-dimension observational analysis
items.abstract: BackgroundErgonomic problems are common in the field of dentistry due to musculoskeletal and neurological conditions that occur in various parts of the body as a result of poor posture and repetitive movements.ObjectivesTo analyze ergonomic errors by clinical area among dental students at a private university in Cusco.MethodsA cross-sectional observational study using secondary data was conducted, involving a population of 182 students selected according to specific criteria. A sample of 150 students from different areas of the dental clinic at a private university in Cusco, corresponding to the seventh, eighth, and ninth semesters, was analyzed. The RULA and REBA ergonomic scales were applied as assessment tools.ResultsThe study revealed that poor postures predominated in the pediatric dentistry clinical area across the five dimensions analyzed, followed by endodontics, restorative dentistry, periodontics, and oral rehabilitation.ConclusionsThere is a high prevalence of poor posture among dental students, highlighting the need for ergonomic education and preventive measures to reduce musculoskeletal injuries and improve the well-being of future dentists, regardless of their specialty.

items.title: Prediction of postoperative persistent pain after rotator cuff repair based on psychological measurements via machine learning
items.abstract: Abstract Background With the development of artificial intelligence technique, machine learning (ML) algorithms have been widely applied to forecast outcomes of various diseases. Current study aimed to investigate the potential utility of machine learning algorithms for predicting postoperative persistent shoulder pain (PSP) and to investigate the related risk factors following rotator cuff repair surgery. Materials and methods A cohort of 491 patients with rotator cuff tears who had undergone surgical intervention was enrolled and analyzed. Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score of ≥4 at one year follow-up was defined as indicative of ongoing shoulder pain. Consequently, patients were classified into a residual pain group and a pain-free group. Nine commonly used machine learning models were trained to distinguish between patients with residual pain and those without. Furthermore, the three models that exhibited the highest predictive performance were combined into a single ensemble of the nine models to improve the classification of patients with residual pain versus those without. The area under the curve (AUC), specificity, sensitivity and accuracy were calculated for each model to evaluate their predictive capabilities. A prespecified LASSO-based feature-selection strategy was used to identify candidate clinical variables, with additional stability analyses (forward selection, exhaustive search) reported in the Supplementary Materials. Variables consistently selected were considered candidate risk factors for PSP in patients. Results (1) Machine learning models demonstrated their effectiveness in classifying patients with postoperative pain. The predictive performance was notably enhanced using an ensemble learning technique. Among the models, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) exhibited the highest accuracy when serving as the aggregator. (2) The ensemble learning models identified several critical predictive factors, including the Fear of Pain Questionnaire, the Pain Catastrophizing Scale, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)-Perceived Sleep Quality, the Central Sensitization Inventory, and the Pain Surface Body Chart score. Conclusion Our findings suggest that a stacking ensemble of preoperative psychosocial variables, developed and internally validated in this single-center retrospective cohort, shows promise for preliminary risk stratification of clinically significant shoulder pain at one year after rotator cuff repair. These hypothesis-generating results require multicenter external validation before clinical use. Level of evidence Level 4, Diagnosis. Clinical trial number Not applicable. This was a retrospective observational study and was not registered as a clinical trial.

items.title: Preparing for emerging risks: AI, cyber governance, and nuclear security cooperation in Southeast Asia
items.abstract: This Perspective article examines the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ (ASEAN) initiatives to strengthen artificial intelligence (AI) and cyber security governance and explores their potential to reinforce nuclear security in Southeast Asia. It argues that as digital technologies become increasingly embedded in nuclear facilities and supply chains, integrating cyber security into nuclear security frameworks is imperative. The study recommends the development of a regional action plan or roadmap to (i) embed cyber security more systematically into nuclear security policies, (ii) deepen cooperation among ASEAN member states, and (iii) raise awareness of the AI–cyber–nuclear security nexus among industry, civil society, and academia. The paper also highlights the roles of key regional and international actors, including the ASEAN Network of Regulatory Bodies on Atomic Energy (ASEANTOM), ASEAN cyber security institutions, AI safety think tanks, and Track II expert networks, in advancing cooperation and knowledge-sharing in this emerging domain. Drawing on the author’s experience with the Nuclear Energy Experts Group of the Council for Security Cooperation in the Asia-Pacific (CSCAP), the paper illustrates how Track II dialogues have facilitated the identification of AI–cyber–nuclear security risks, raised awareness among policymakers, scientists, and academics, and informed ongoing discussions on enhancing nuclear security governance in Southeast Asia.

items.title: PROSE: Rubric-Aware Multi-Objective Fine-Tuning of Small Language Models for Automated Assessment of Second-Language Writing
items.abstract: Automated assessment of second-language (L2) writing supports language teaching and testing by providing rapid, consistent scores across multiple rubric dimensions. We study whether small, openly available language models can be turned into reliable analytic raters, and we introduce PROSE, a rubric-aware, multi-objective fine-tuning method built on a compact DeBERTa-v3 encoder with low-rank adaptation. PROSE trains a regression read-out together with a soft-ordinal auxiliary head, and combines a squared-error term for calibration, a distance-aware soft-ordinal term that respects the ordered rubric bands, a concordance term that restores the spread of human ratings and improves agreement with human ratings, and a trait-relational coherence term. On the ELLIPSE corpus of L2 English essays, PROSE raises the quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) from 0.646 for a strong regression baseline to 0.661—a small but statistically reliable gain under a paired test across folds (mean difference +0.015—95% CI [0.007,0.023], and paired t-test p=0.007; p=0.030 after correcting for the overlap between cross-validation training sets), with comparable error and improvements on all seven scoring dimensions, four of which remain significant after Holm correction, and on the Write & Improve (BEA-2019) proficiency data, it matches the strongest baseline on agreement and accuracy and clearly outperforms classification and pure ordinal training. Zero-shot prompting of three strong large language models (GPT-5.4, Claude-Sonnet-4-6, DeepSeek-Chat) reaches a kappa of only 0.13 to 0.21 on the same essays, and a distributional analysis shows that the tested large models produce compressed score distributions with means below the human mean, while the compact fine-tuned model reproduces the human score distribution. Further analyses show that the gain is stable under reasonable changes of the loss weights and holds for truncated and non-truncated essays and across gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic, and grade groups, although these analyses also reveal a shared grade-related bias and a reliance on length and lexical-diversity cues that call for caution in deployment. The results indicate that, for this task, a task-specific objective applied to a small supervised model is far more effective than general-purpose models used zero-shot; we are careful to attribute the gap to task-specific supervision and objective design rather than to model scale alone.

items.title: Psychobiotics and polyphenols modulate the gut-brain axis through personalized nutritional strategies in mental health
items.abstract: Anxiety and depression are major contributors to the global disease burden; however, fewer than half of patients treated with standard pharmacotherapy achieve sustained remission. This gap underscores the need to identify effective adjunctive treatments. The bidirectional gut-brain axis offers a valuable perspective by linking diet to neurotransmission, neuroinflammation, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis reactivity. This framework positions nutritional psychiatry as a complement, rather than a substitute, for established care. This narrative review examines three converging intervention classes: psychobiotics, dietary polyphenols, and precision nutraceuticals. Randomized trials of Lactobacillus helveticus R0052, Bifidobacterium longum R0175, and Lactiplantibacillus plantarum PS128 demonstrate modest but reproducible reductions in depressive and anxiety symptoms, although effect sizes vary. Plausible mechanisms include reduced low-grade neuroinflammation, partial normalization of HPA axis reactivity, and a shift in tryptophan metabolism from the kynurenine pathway toward serotonin synthesis—although human evidence supporting these pathways remains limited. Polyphenol biology introduces an additional dimension. Microbial conversion of ellagitannins, isoflavones, and lignans into urolithin A, equol, and enterolactone can alter the bioavailability of neuroactive metabolites. Consequently, an individual’s metabotype likely accounts for some of the variability in clinical response. We propose that microbiota-guided strategies—stratified by enterotype, metabotype, tryptophan–kynurenine flux, and short-chain fatty acid output—could significantly enhance psychiatric care. Multi-omic profiling and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven digital phenotyping can operationalize this precision approach. However, methodological heterogeneity, small sample sizes, inconsistent strain and dose reporting, and regulatory ambiguity continue to hinder translation, as recent meta-analyses highlight.

items.title: Psychological pathways to responsible generative AI decision-making among teachers: governance clarity, perceived accountability, decision uncertainty, and AI literacy
items.abstract: Introduction Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can assist teachers with organizing information, generating alternatives, and drafting feedback. Its use in consequential judgments requires verifiable evidence and professional oversight. This study examines how teachers regulate optional GenAI assistance while preserving professional judgment. Methods Research on felt accountability, metacognitive monitoring, and AI literacy is conceptually integrated to develop a psychological process model of teacher decision episodes. Governance clarity is specified through rule clarity and role clarity, with responsible GenAI decision-making defined as regulated decision conduct. Results The conceptual analysis produces five testable propositions and one configurational expectation. Governance clarity is proposed to support responsible conduct through perceived accountability. Decision uncertainty is modeled as a metacognitive signal whose behavioral value depends on calibration and regulation; AI literacy is specified as a resource for verification, calibrated reliance, and appropriate escalation. Responsible conduct encompasses appropriate delegation, verification, calibrated reliance and accountable human authority, traceability, and escalation or override. These model outputs are theoretical propositions, not empirically established effects. Discussion The framework distinguishes generative assistance from conventional algorithmic advice and identifies task-dependent applications in assessment, feedback, referral, and student support. Future tests should compare unaided and assisted judgment, distinguish process quality from decision accuracy, and examine stakes, reversibility, and contextual dependence. Teachers retain authority to accept, modify, or reject GenAI output, or proceed without GenAI assistance.

items.title: Receipts, Not Vibes: A Single-Operator Measurement of AI-Native Build Velocity (v1.1)
items.abstract: A measurement, not an argument, in the vibe-coding debate. Over a closed 33-day window (2026-09-24 to 2026-10-26) a single operator working with AI agents produced, in publicly re-derivable form: 383 append-only transparency-ledger entries, 117 Zenodo publications minted in October 2026 (207 records in the full public corpus: 155 open access, 52 restricted), 61 closed adversarial and containment test series, and 13 patent filings. The note defines audit velocity as the rate at which a human-plus-deterministic-journal system converts intent into verifiable shipped state. v1.1 CORRECTION DISCLOSURE: three figures changed and one date was corrected after re-derivation on 2026-10-28. Ledger rows moved 376 to 383 because the 2026-10-27 ledger-regression repair restored eight previously published lines that a stale-base push had dropped (correction receipt 0362). October mints moved 116 to 117 and the corpus figure moved from 159 to 207 because the authoritative source is the owner account's Zenodo deposit listing, not a keyword search that excluded access-restricted records and creator-name variants. The corpus start date moved from 2026-04-10 to 2026-04-01. The v1.0 figures are disclosed in a table in section 4.1 rather than silently overwritten. SCOPE LIMITS, STATED IN THE PAPER: not a quality claim; N=1 with no control; not a method paper (playbooks and hypervisor internals remain private); and it is itself an AI-assisted artifact produced inside the journal it measures. The accompanying dataset itemises the 155 open-access records only. Restricted records are counted in aggregate so that archive inventory the author chose to restrict is not disclosed. Two-key curation: drafted and vetted by the operator's agent system (Gabriel); owner authorization Leon GO (chat authorization, 2026-10-28 09:54 CT) for documentation surfaces (Zenodo and GitHub). No social-media posting accompanies this record. Prototype disclaimer: this software and its measurements are prototypes provided for educational and research purposes only. They are not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects.

items.title: Reference Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: The advancement of Generative AI (GenAI) technology has revolutionized the digital marketing sector, yet its impact on consumer psychology requires deeper understanding. Employing a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach based on the Scopus database, this study analyzes the relationships among GenAI usage, customer engagement, and customer trust. Literature mapping reveals that current research focuses on four primary clusters: consumer behavioral dynamics and purchase intentions, visual quality (hyperrealism), transparency and ethical issues, and collaborative creativity efficiency. Based on an analysis of these findings, the study identifies an "Authenticity Paradox," wherein AI-generated hyperrealistic visuals effectively boost purchase intentions but risk triggering the "uncanny valley" effect thereby undermining consumer trust if transparency is lacking. Trust is significantly shaped by the interplay between drivers, such as transparent labeling (watermarking), and inhibitors, such as visual artifacts and privacy concerns. Regarding engagement effectiveness, AI proves superior in stimulating interaction among existing followers, whereas human-generated content remains essential for reaching new audiences due to its empathy and emotional resonance. The study concludes that adopting a hybrid marketing strategy specifically Human-AI Co-Creation represents the optimal approach for synergizing GenAI's technological efficiency with the authenticity of the human touch in the long term.
